method_card.title: Physical Wellbeing — Body, Illness and Health
method_card.content:
This lesson covers body parts, describing symptoms with doler, common illnesses, and giving health advice. A key setting for this topic is the doctor's surgery — one of the prescribed transactional settings in the speaking exam.

SpanishEnglish
la cabezahead
el estómagostomach
la gargantathroat
el brazoarm
la piernaleg
la espaldaback
me duelemy ... hurts (singular)
me duelenmy ... hurt (plural)
tengo fiebreI have a fever
tengo tosI have a cough
estoy enfermo/aI am ill
un resfriadoa cold
la gripethe flu
el medicamentomedicine
hay que + infinitiveone must / it is necessary to

Grammar focus — doler: Doler works like gustar: use me duele + singular body part, me duelen + plural body part. The verb agrees with the body part, not the person. Me duele la garganta (My throat hurts), me duelen los pies (My feet hurt).

Grammar focus — tener for health: Spanish uses tener for conditions where English uses 'to be': tengo fiebre (I have a fever), tengo tos (I have a cough). Use estar for general illness: estoy enfermo/a (I am ill — temporary state, so estar not ser).

Model: Me duele la garganta y tengo fiebre. Estoy muy cansado. Hay que tomar medicamentos y descansar en casa. (My throat hurts and I have a fever. I am very tired. One must take medicine and rest at home.)
steps: Learn key body part vocabulary — note the gender of each noun
Master me duele (singular) vs me duelen (plural) for describing pain
Use tener for health conditions: tengo fiebre, tengo tos, tengo un resfriado
Practice the doctor's surgery role-play using hay que + infinitive for advice

exam_context.frequency: Common in listening and reading comprehension; doctor's surgery is a prescribed speaking setting

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: Me duelen las piernas y no puedo caminar.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Me duelen (plural — duelen not duele) because las piernas is plural.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: no puedo caminar = I can't walk. Poder + infinitive.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: My legs hurt and I can't walk.

worked_examples.question: Choose duele or duelen: 'Me ___ los ojos.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Look at the body part: los ojos (the eyes) — this is plural.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Plural body parts use duelen. Singular body parts use duele.

bronze.question: Match the Spanish body parts to their English meaning
Match the Spanish illness phrases to their English meaning

gaps.correct_explain: duele (singular) because la cabeza is singular. Me duele = it hurts me.

wrong.duelen: duelen is plural. La cabeza is singular → me duele.
wrong.dolor: dolor is the noun (pain), not the verb. You need the verb → duele.

gaps.correct_explain: tengo fiebre = I have a fever. Spanish uses tener (not ser/estar) for fever.

wrong.estoy: estoy means 'I am'. In Spanish, fever uses tener: tengo fiebre.

bronze.question: Complete the sentence
sentence_parts: los pies porque he caminado mucho

wrong.duele: duele is singular. Los pies is plural → me duelen.

gaps.correct_explain: hoy = today. This fits the context of having walked a lot.

wrong.ayer: ayer (yesterday) would also work but changes the time reference — the perfect tense he caminado is most natural with hoy.

bronze.question: Which sentence correctly says 'My throat hurts'?

bronze.source_text: Estoy enfermo. Me duele el estómago y tengo náuseas. Necesito ir al médico.
model_answers: I am ill. My stomach hurts and I feel nauseous. I need to go to the doctor.

bronze.question: Listen and type what you hear
bronze.audio_text: Me duele la cabeza y estoy cansado.
bronze.correct_text: Me duele la cabeza y estoy cansado.
bronze.translation: My head hurts and I am tired.

silver.question: Complete the sentence
sentence_parts: duele la espalda y tiene que
silver.english: His back hurts and he has to take medicine.

gaps.correct_explain: Le is the indirect object pronoun for 'him/her'. Le duele = his/her... hurts.

wrong.Se: Se is reflexive. For doler, use indirect object pronouns: le for him/her.

gaps.correct_explain: tomar is the infinitive. After tener que, always use the infinitive.

wrong.toma: toma is conjugated. After tener que, use the infinitive → tomar.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: Me duele los ojos y no puedo leer.
silver.explanation: Los ojos is plural, so the verb must be duelen (not duele). Doler agrees with the body part.
silver.translation: My eyes hurt and I can't read.

silver.question: Build the sentence in Spanish
silver.english: I need to go to the doctor because my throat hurts.

distractor_labels.duelen: wrong number — la garganta is singular, so duele not duelen

silver.source_text: I don't feel well. My stomach hurts and I have a fever. I have to rest.
model_answers: No me siento bien. Me duele el estómago y tengo fiebre. Tengo que descansar.
hints: I don't feel well = no me siento bien

silver.audio_text: Tengo que tomar medicamentos porque tengo un resfriado.
silver.correct_text: Tengo que tomar medicamentos porque tengo un resfriado.
silver.translation: I have to take medicine because I have a cold.

silver.question: Put these words in the correct order to form a sentence

gold.source_text: My mother is ill today. She has a bad headache and is very tired. She is going to stay at home to rest. My brother fell and hurt his leg. He has to go to hospital.
model_answers: Mi madre está enferma hoy. Tiene mucho dolor de cabeza y está muy cansada. Va a quedarse en casa para descansar. Mi hermano se cayó y se hizo daño en la pierna. Tiene que ir al hospital.
gold.ai_system_prompt: You are a GCSE Spanish examiner marking a translation about illness and injury. Source: '{source}'. Model answer: '{model}'. Check: estar for illness and tiredness (not ser), tener for symptoms (dolor de cabeza), near future (va a + infinitive), preterite for past event (se cayó), tener que + infinitive. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences","improvement":"optional correction"}

gold.question: Build the sentence in Spanish
gold.english: My legs hurt and I can't walk. I have to go to the hospital.

distractor_labels.duele: wrong number — las piernas is plural, so duelen not duele
distractor_labels.puede: wrong person — puede is él/ella. The subject is 'I' → puedo
distractor_labels.pierna: wrong number — the English says 'legs' (plural) → piernas

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are visiting Spain and feel unwell. You go to the doctor's surgery.

bullets.model_answer: Me duele la garganta y me duelen los oídos.
bullets.note: me duele + singular; me duelen + plural

bullets.model_answer: También tengo fiebre y estoy muy cansado. No me siento bien.
bullets.note: tener for fever + estar for tiredness (temporary states, not ser)

bullets.prompt: Say what you think caused the illness.
bullets.model_answer: Creo que me mojé en la lluvia ayer y dormí poco.
bullets.note: creo que + preterite; me mojé (I got wet), dormí (I slept)

bullets.prompt: Ask the doctor what you need to do.

gold.ai_system_prompt: You are a GCSE Spanish examiner marking a doctor's surgery role play. For each bullet, assess: (1) Did the student communicate the required information? (2) Is the Spanish grammatically accurate? Check: doler singular/plural, tener for conditions (not ser/estar for fever), estar for temporary states (estoy cansado), question formation. Award marks out of 10. Be encouraging. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"Per-bullet feedback","improvement":"Key grammar point"}

gold.question: Write 40-50 words in Spanish about a time you were ill. Include: what hurt, what symptoms you had, whether you went to the doctor, and what you had to do to get better.
gold.ai_system_prompt: You are a GCSE Spanish examiner marking extended writing about illness. Mark on: Communication (all points addressed?), Range of language (doler singular/plural, tener for conditions, preterite for past events, modal verbs + infinitive), Accuracy (doler agreement, tener not ser/estar for fever/conditions, estar not ser for tiredness/illness). Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"3-4 sentences","improvement":"One grammar point"}

gold.question: Listen and type what you hear
gold.audio_text: Mi madre está enferma hoy. Le duele la cabeza y tiene fiebre. Va a ir al médico para recibir medicamentos.
gold.correct_text: Mi madre está enferma hoy. Le duele la cabeza y tiene fiebre. Va a ir al médico para recibir medicamentos.
gold.translation: My mother is ill today. Her head hurts and she has a fever. She is going to go to the doctor to get medicine.

gold.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
gold.sentence: Estoy enferma desde ayer. Soy muy cansada y tengo tos.
gold.explanation: Tiredness is a temporary state, so you must use estar, not ser. Estoy muy cansada = I am very tired. Ser is for permanent traits; estar is for moods, feelings and temporary conditions.
gold.translation: I have been ill since yesterday. I am very tired and I have a cough.
